metadata.note: The Sunbury and Lewistown Railroad (Selinsgrove Junction - Middleburg - Beavertown - McClure - Lewistown, PA, opened 1871), worked from opening by the Pennsylvania Railroad as its Lewistown Branch until passenger service ended in January 1932. One feature. Research report: research/branches/sunbury_and_lewistown_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-22).
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952)
metadata.operator_split: None. The PRR lease (agreement Oct 20 1871) predates the regular opening (Nov 13 / Dec 1 1871), so the PRR ran every confirmed passenger year: one PRR feature in PRR colour. The 1874 sheriff's sale, 1876 reorganisation, 1896 consolidation with the Mifflin & Centre County, 1900 merger into the Schuylkill & Juniata and 1902 merger into the PRR changed ownership, not who ran the trains. Baer's 'Oct.? 1871' mixed train Lewistown - Beavertown may predate the lease and its operator is not stated; no separate Sunbury and Lewistown feature is drawn, as that would assert an S&L-operated year nobody has shown.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1). Excluded: everything after the last passenger train of Jan 16 1932 - PRR through freight to 1953 and locals after; Maitland - Paxtonville (lifted 1958-65) and Paxtonville - Kreamer (abandoned Apr 1976); Selinsgrove Jct - Kreamer (Conrail, NS, SEDA-COG / North Shore RR) and Lewistown Jct - Maitland (SEDA-COG / Juniata Valley RR from 1996), still freight today; the PP&L power-plant spur (1945+) at the west end of the river bridge. Undated post-1932 charters and detours (Britton, unverified) are not drawn.
metadata.omitted: Sunbury - Selinsgrove Junction is Northern Central main line, already drawn by 'Northern Central: Baltimore - Elmira' (pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson); not re-drawn. The PRR Milroy Branch (ex Mifflin & Centre County, Lewistown - Reedsville - Milroy), corporately part of the S&L Railway only 1896-1900, is a separate road outside this report and is not drawn here; OSM tags it with the same note:old_railway_operator='Schuylkill and Juniata', and the trace was kept off it.
not_yet_sourced: 1874-1876 hiatus: Wikipedia says the railroad 'ceased to operate' soon after opening and was sold at sheriff's sale May 1874, the PRR 'assuming operation' on reorganisation Feb 1 1876; Fowler dates station names to the 1874 Official Guide (Kremer, Meiser's) and an 1875 PRR public timetable (Shindel, Rager's Summit), i.e. passenger trains advertised in that interval. Not reconciled - Baer's 1874-1876 chronologies are not online at the PRRTHS path. Drawn continuous 1871-1932; if a source shows passenger service actually suspended, the segment needs a gap.

First through crossing of the Susquehanna: Baer's opening entries say 'between Selinsgrove and Lewistown Jct', and completion of the east end was contingent on the Selinsgrove Bridge (first bridge wooden; oldest surviving parts 1888). The date the first train crossed to Selinsgrove Junction / Sunbury is not established; the river leg is drawn from 1871 with the rest and may be a little early.
Opening day: Nov 13 1871 (Watkins) vs Dec 1 1871 (PRR Annual Report, valuation, Railroad Gazette), both via Baer. Same year either way.

End date rests on the PRRTHS discontinuance list (entry not asterisked 'believed correct') and Wikipedia (uncited; Britton copies Wikipedia). A Sunbury Daily Item / Lewistown Sentinel 'last train' story would settle January 1932.
headway_min (360) and avg_speed_kmh (30) are estimates: Wikipedia's 'two trains each way a day except on Sundays' is undated, and no running time was found.
Post-1932 passenger charters and detours (Britton): undated, unverified, not drawn.
Mileage: 44.5 (Fowler, Selinsgrove Jct - Lewistown 2nd) vs 44 (state marker) vs '43 1/2' (unsourced web summary) vs ~50 (Wikipedia, from Sunbury). The trace (44.47 mi) supports Fowler.

properties.speed_source: estimate, not sourced: no Lewistown Branch running time was found for any year; a figure typical of a PRR steam branch local with frequent stops
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR + note:old_railway_operator='Schuylkill and Juniata' (e.g. live 116268193, 12000637, 12048004, 12048000, 161391959; abandoned 143470443, 143470442, 143470441, 143472082, 143472086, 143351879, 143351874; live 1017461879, 143351882, 14236437, 170400522), routed with opstrace.py (note:old_railway_operator counted as the operator tag), Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals. OpenHistoricalMap and OSM rail-trail ways were fetched for Maitland - Kreamer but not needed: the OSM abandoned grade is continuous.
properties.geometry_quality: Selinsgrove Junction - Lewistown Junction: 44.47 mi drawn against 44.5 mi documented (Fowler PRR section 40 mileposts, Selinsgrove Junction 5.0 - Lewistown (2nd) 49.5 from Sunbury), -0.1 %. No approximated (straight-line) legs. The whole 44.5 mi is real-traced on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR + note:old_railway_operator='Schuylkill and Juniata' (the S&L's 1900-02 successor company), opstrace mileage by operator: 44.5 mi on those ways, nothing else. Of that, about 7.8 mi Selinsgrove Jct - Kreamer is live track (SEDA-COG / North Shore RR), including the Susquehanna crossing on the Selinsgrove Bridge; about 30.7 mi Kreamer - east of Maitland is the lifted grade (railway=abandoned, partly road/lane alignments such as Railroad Street, Beavertown); about 5.9 mi Maitland - Lewistown Junction is live track (Juniata Valley RR, way 170400522 at the junction). The line starts on the junction node with the NS Buffalo Line (ex Northern Central) on the east bank (OSM node 108490080, 14 m from the existing Northern Central feature) and ends on the junction node with the main line at Lewistown Junction (node 136267222, 94 m from the existing PRR Main Line feature). Waypoint fit: Selinsgrove 0.2 km, Kreamer 0.8 (village centre; the line passes its south edge), Middleburg 0.2, Paxtonville 0.4, Beavertown 0.2, Beaver Springs 0.3, McClure 0.1, Maitland 0.1, Lewistown borough on the line. ERA: the drawn line is the surviving / last alignment - the live ends as rebuilt for modern freight and the abandoned grade as last used (Penn Central / Conrail); the river crossing is the present Selinsgrove Bridge, whose oldest parts date from 1888, not the original wooden bridge, and the Lewistown street running (Chestnut Street) is drawn as OSM now maps it. No relocation of the line is known, but none was checked for.

segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad Lewistown Branch (the Sunbury and Lewistown Railroad, PRR-leased under agreement of Oct 20 1871): Selinsgrove Junction (Northern Central, east bank of the Susquehanna) - Selinsgrove Bridge - Selinsgrove - Kreamer - Middleburg - Paxtonville - Beavertown - Beaver Springs - McClure - Maitland - Lewistown (Walnut St, Main St) - Lewistown Junction (PRR Main Line station). Trains ran through to and from Sunbury over 5 mi of Northern Central track (drawn by 'Northern Central: Baltimore - Elmira', not here). START 1871: a mixed train Lewistown - Beavertown from c. Sept/Oct 1871 (Baer, citing USRR&MR / Guide 'prob 9/71'); regular service Selinsgrove - Lewistown Jct from Nov 13 1871 (Watkins) or Dec 1 1871 (PRR Annual Report, valuation, Railroad Gazette), all via Baer - the same year every way, and the PRR lease predates the regular opening, so the PRR ran the regular trains from day one. When the first through train crossed the river to Selinsgrove Jct is NOT established (see metadata.not_yet_sourced); the river leg is drawn from 1871 with the rest. END 1932: last passenger train Jan 16 1932 (PRRTHS discontinuance list, 'Selinsgrove Jct.-Lewistown - 1/16/1932', an entry the compiler did NOT asterisk as 'believed correct'; Wikipedia 'January 1932', uncited). The Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggers Kreamer, Middleburg, Beavertown and Selinsgrove 'for freight only' - consistent, not independent proof of the year. Corporate changes that did not change who ran the trains (not Rule 4 splits): sheriff's sale May 1874, reorganised as the Sunbury & Lewistown Railway Feb 1 1876, merged with the Mifflin & Centre County Oct 1 1896, into the Schuylkill & Juniata Jun 1 1900, into the PRR Apr 1 1902. Wikipedia says the company 'ceased to operate' around the 1874 sale, but Fowler dates station names to the 1874 Official Guide and an 1875 PRR public timetable, so passenger trains were advertised in that interval; drawn continuous, conflict recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced. Service 'typically ... two trains each way a day except on Sundays' (Wikipedia, era unstated): headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE from that, not a timetable figure. The line was also a heavy PRR freight cutoff (up to 70 trains a day before the Sept 1908 diversion to the Bald Eagle line). After 1932 (not drawn, Rule 1): occasional charters and detours (Britton, unverified, undated); through freight to 1953; Maitland - Paxtonville lifted 1958-65; Paxtonville - Kreamer abandoned Apr 1976; Selinsgrove Jct - Kreamer (NS, then SEDA-COG / North Shore RR from 2022) and Lewistown Jct - Maitland (SEDA-COG / Juniata Valley RR from 1996) remain freight-only.
sources: Segment-level: opening Nov 13 / Dec 1 1871 and PRR lease Oct 20 1871 from Baer PRR Chronology 1871; last passenger train 16 Jan 1932 from PRRTHS discontinuance list (unasterisked) and Wikipedia. headway_min is NOT SOURCED (estimate from Wikipedia's undated 'two trains each way a day').
